title: Vocal Prognostic Digital Biomarkers in Monitoring Chronic Heart Failure: A Longitudinal Observational Study
summary:
Objective: This study aimed to evaluate which voice features can predict health deterioration in patients with chronic HF.
  Background: Heart failure (HF) is a chronic condition with progressive deterioration and acute decompensations, often requiring hospitalization and imposing substantial healthcare and economic burdens. Current standard-of-care (SoC) home monitoring, such as weight tracking, lacks predictive accuracy and requires high patient engagement. Voice is a promising non-invasive biomarker, though prior studies have mainly focused on acute HF stages.
  Methods: In a 2-month longitudinal study, 32 patients with HF collected daily voice recordings and SoC measures of weight and blood pressure at home, with biweekly questionnaires for health status. Acoustic analysis generated detailed vowel and speech features. Time-series features were extracted from aggregated lookback windows (e.g., 7 days) to predict next-day health status. Explainable machine learning with nested cross-validation identified top vocal biomarkers, and a case study illustrated model application.
  Results: A total of 21,863 recordings were analyzed. Acoustic vowel features showed strong correlations with health status. Time-series voice features within the lookback window outperformed corresponding standard care measures, achieving peak sensitivity and specificity of 0.826 and 0.782 versus 0.783 and 0.567 for SoC metrics. Key prognostic voice features identifying deterioration included delayed energy shift, low energy variability, and higher shimmer variability in vowels, along with reduced speaking and articulation rate, lower phonation ratio, decreased voice quality, and increased formant variability in speech.
  Conclusion: Voice-based monitoring offers a non-invasive approach to detect early health changes in chronic HF, supporting proactive and personalized care.

AI.tldr: Voice features from daily recordings predict health deterioration in chronic heart failure patients better than standard care measures like weight tracking.
AI.motivation: Heart failure is a chronic progressive condition with frequent acute decompensations requiring hospitalization. Current standard-of-care home monitoring (weight tracking) lacks predictive accuracy and requires high patient engagement. Voice shows promise as a non-invasive biomarker, but prior studies focused mainly on acute HF stages rather than chronic monitoring.
AI.method: 2-month longitudinal study with 32 HF patients collecting daily voice recordings alongside standard care measures (weight, blood pressure) and biweekly health status questionnaires. Acoustic analysis generated detailed vowel and speech features. Time-series features were extracted from aggregated lookback windows (e.g., 7 days) to predict next-day health status. Used explainable machine learning with nested cross-validation to identify top vocal biomarkers, with case study illustration.
AI.result: Analyzed 21,863 recordings. Acoustic vowel features strongly correlated with health status. Time-series voice features within lookback windows outperformed standard care measures: peak sensitivity/specificity of 0.826/0.782 for voice vs. 0.783/0.567 for SoC metrics. Key prognostic voice features included delayed energy shift, low energy variability, higher shimmer variability in vowels, reduced speaking/articulation rate, lower phonation ratio, decreased voice quality, and increased formant variability in speech.
AI.conclusion: Voice-based monitoring offers a non-invasive approach to detect early health changes in chronic HF, supporting proactive and personalized care.

title: Sona: Real-Time Multi-Target Sound Attenuation for Noise Sensitivity
summary: For people with noise sensitivity, everyday soundscapes can be overwhelming. Existing tools such as active noise cancellation reduce discomfort by suppressing the entire acoustic environment, often at the cost of awareness of surrounding people and events. We present Sona, an interactive mobile system for real-time soundscape mediation that selectively attenuates bothersome sounds while preserving desired audio. Sona is built on a target-conditioned neural pipeline that supports simultaneous attenuation of multiple overlapping sound sources, overcoming the single-target limitation of prior systems. It runs in real time on-device and supports user-extensible sound classes through in-situ audio examples, without retraining. Sona is informed by a formative study with 68 noise-sensitive individuals. Through technical benchmarking and an in-situ study with 10 participants, we show that Sona achieves low-latency, multi-target attenuation suitable for live listening, and enables meaningful reductions in bothersome sounds while maintaining awareness of surroundings. These results point toward a new class of personal AI systems that support comfort and social participation by mediating real-world acoustic environments.

AI.tldr: Sona is a real-time mobile soundscape mediation system that selectively attenuates bothersome sounds while preserving desired audio using a target-conditioned neural pipeline, enabling multi-target attenuation and user-extensible sound classes without retraining.
AI.motivation: Existing noise cancellation tools suppress entire acoustic environments, reducing awareness of surrounding people and events. People with noise sensitivity need selective attenuation of bothersome sounds while maintaining desired audio for social participation and comfort.
AI.method: Sona uses a target-conditioned neural pipeline supporting simultaneous attenuation of multiple overlapping sound sources. It runs real-time on-device and allows user-extensible sound classes through in-situ audio examples without retraining. The system was informed by a formative study with 68 noise-sensitive individuals.
AI.result: Technical benchmarking and in-situ study with 10 participants show Sona achieves low-latency, multi-target attenuation suitable for live listening. It enables meaningful reductions in bothersome sounds while maintaining awareness of surroundings.
AI.conclusion: Sona represents a new class of personal AI systems that mediate real-world acoustic environments to support comfort and social participation through selective sound attenuation.

title: TRACE: Training-Free Partial Audio Deepfake Detection via Embedding Trajectory Analysis of Speech Foundation Models
summary: Partial audio deepfakes, where synthesized segments are spliced into genuine recordings, are particularly deceptive because most of the audio remains authentic. Existing detectors are supervised: they require frame-level annotations, overfit to specific synthesis pipelines, and must be retrained as new generative models emerge. We argue that this supervision is unnecessary. We hypothesize that speech foundation models implicitly encode a forensic signal: genuine speech forms smooth, slowly varying embedding trajectories, while splice boundaries introduce abrupt disruptions in frame-level transitions. Building on this, we propose TRACE (Training-free Representation-based Audio Countermeasure via Embedding dynamics), a training-free framework that detects partial audio deepfakes by analyzing the first-order dynamics of frozen speech foundation model representations without any training, labeled data, or architectural modification. We evaluate TRACE on four benchmarks that span two languages using six speech foundation models. In PartialSpoof, TRACE achieves 8.08% EER, competitive with fine-tuned supervised baselines. In LlamaPartialSpoof, the most challenging benchmark featuring LLM-driven commercial synthesis, TRACE surpasses a supervised baseline outright (24.12% vs. 24.49% EER) without any target-domain data. These results show that temporal dynamics in speech foundation models provide an effective, generalize signal for training-free audio forensics.

AI.tldr: TRACE is a training-free framework that detects partial audio deepfakes by analyzing abrupt disruptions in embedding trajectories from frozen speech foundation models, achieving competitive performance with supervised methods without requiring training data or annotations.
AI.motivation: Existing partial audio deepfake detectors require frame-level annotations, overfit to specific synthesis pipelines, and need retraining for new generative models. The authors hypothesize that speech foundation models implicitly encode forensic signals through smooth embedding trajectories for genuine speech versus abrupt disruptions at splice boundaries.
AI.method: TRACE (Training-free Representation-based Audio Countermeasure via Embedding dynamics) analyzes first-order dynamics of frozen speech foundation model representations without any training, labeled data, or architectural modification. It detects partial audio deepfakes by identifying abrupt disruptions in frame-level embedding transitions at splice boundaries.
AI.result: On PartialSpoof benchmark, TRACE achieves 8.08% EER, competitive with fine-tuned supervised baselines. On LlamaPartialSpoof (most challenging benchmark with LLM-driven commercial synthesis), TRACE surpasses supervised baseline (24.12% vs. 24.49% EER) without any target-domain data. Evaluated across four benchmarks spanning two languages using six speech foundation models.
AI.conclusion: Temporal dynamics in speech foundation models provide an effective, generalize signal for training-free audio forensics. The approach eliminates need for supervision, frame-level annotations, and retraining for new synthesis methods, offering a practical solution for detecting partial audio deepfakes.

title: Description and Discussion on DCASE 2026 Challenge Task 4: Spatial Semantic Segmentation of Sound Scenes
summary: This paper presents an overview of the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) 2026 Challenge Task 4, Spatial Semantic Segmentation of Sound Scenes (S5). The S5 task focuses on the joint detection and separation of sound events in complex spatial audio mixtures, contributing to the foundation of immersive communication. First introduced in DCASE 2025, the S5 task continues in DCASE 2026 Task 4 with key changes to better reflect real-world conditions, including allowing mixtures to contain multiple sources of the same class and to contain no target sources. In this paper, we describe task setting, along with the corresponding updates to the evaluation metrics and dataset. The experimental results of the submitted systems are also reported and analyzed. The official access point for data and code is https://github.com/nttcslab/dcase2026_task4_baseline.

AI.tldr: DCASE 2026 Task 4 (S5) focuses on spatial semantic segmentation of sound scenes for joint detection and separation of sound events in complex spatial audio mixtures, with updates to better reflect real-world conditions.
AI.motivation: To advance immersive communication by developing systems that can jointly detect and separate sound events in complex spatial audio mixtures, addressing real-world challenges like multiple sources of the same class and absence of target sources.
AI.method: The paper describes the task setting for DCASE 2026 Task 4 (S5), including updates to evaluation metrics and dataset to better reflect real-world conditions. It continues from DCASE 2025 with key changes allowing mixtures to contain multiple sources of the same class and potentially no target sources.
AI.result: The paper reports and analyzes experimental results of submitted systems for the S5 task, though specific performance metrics are not detailed in the abstract. The official baseline code and data are available at https://github.com/nttcslab/dcase2026_task4_baseline.
AI.conclusion: The DCASE 2026 Task 4 (S5) continues to advance spatial semantic segmentation of sound scenes with improved task settings that better reflect real-world audio conditions, providing a benchmark for developing immersive communication systems.

title: Contracting Neural Networks: Sharp LMI Conditions with Applications to Integral Control and Deep Learning
summary: This paper studies contractivity of firing-rate and Hopfield recurrent neural networks. We derive sharp LMI conditions on the synaptic matrices that characterize contractivity of both architectures, for activation functions that are either non-expansive or monotone non-expansive, in both continuous and discrete time. We establish structural relationships among these conditions, including connections to Schur diagonal stability and the recovery of optimal contraction rates for symmetric synaptic matrices. We demonstrate the utility of these results through two applications. First, we develop an LMI-based design procedure for low-gain integral controllers enabling reference tracking in contracting firing rate networks. Second, we provide an exact parameterization of weight matrices that guarantee contraction and use it to improve the expressivity of Implicit Neural Networks, achieving competitive performance on image classification benchmarks with fewer parameters.

AI.tldr: The paper derives sharp LMI conditions for contractivity of firing-rate and Hopfield neural networks, establishes structural relationships, and demonstrates applications in controller design and Implicit Neural Networks.
AI.motivation: To establish rigorous contractivity conditions for recurrent neural networks (firing-rate and Hopfield) that can be used for stability analysis, controller design, and improving neural network expressivity.
AI.method: Derives Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI) conditions for contractivity of both architectures, considering non-expansive or monotone non-expansive activation functions in continuous and discrete time. Establishes connections to Schur diagonal stability and recovers optimal contraction rates for symmetric synaptic matrices.
AI.result: Develops sharp LMI conditions characterizing contractivity, establishes structural relationships among conditions, demonstrates applications: 1) LMI-based design of low-gain integral controllers for reference tracking in contracting firing rate networks, 2) Exact parameterization of weight matrices guaranteeing contraction used to improve Implicit Neural Networks expressivity with competitive performance on image classification benchmarks using fewer parameters.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides comprehensive contractivity analysis for recurrent neural networks with practical applications in control design and neural network architecture optimization, demonstrating the utility of LMI-based approaches for stability and performance guarantees.

title: FineLAP: Taming Heterogeneous Supervision for Fine-grained Language-Audio Pretraining
summary: Contrastively pretrained audio-language models (e.g., CLAP) excel at clip-level understanding but struggle with frame-level tasks. Existing extensions fail to exploit the varying granularity of real-world audio-text data, where massive clip-level textual descriptions coexist with limited frame-level annotations. This paper proposes Fine-grained Language-Audio Pretraining (FineLAP), a novel training paradigm that advances both clip- and frame-level alignment in CLAP with heterogeneous data. FineLAP introduces a dual-stream sigmoid loss with a cluster-based sampling strategy to jointly learn from clip- and frame-level supervision. To capture both global semantics and local details, FineLAP uses a decoupled audio projector on top of a self-supervised encoder. To alleviate the scarcity of temporally annotated data, we present FineLAP-100k, a large-scale synthetic SED dataset constructed through a scalable curation pipeline. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FineLAP achieves SOTA performance across multiple audio understanding tasks, including retrieval, classification, sound event detection, and text-to-audio grounding. Ablation studies further show that coarse- and fine-grained alignment are mutually beneficial, providing insights for building better audio-language models (ALMs).

AI.tldr: FineLAP is a novel audio-language pretraining method that improves both clip-level and frame-level alignment using heterogeneous data, achieving state-of-the-art performance across multiple audio understanding tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing contrastively pretrained audio-language models like CLAP excel at clip-level understanding but struggle with frame-level tasks. Current extensions fail to exploit the varying granularity of real-world audio-text data where massive clip-level descriptions coexist with limited frame-level annotations.
AI.method: FineLAP introduces a dual-stream sigmoid loss with cluster-based sampling to jointly learn from clip- and frame-level supervision. It uses a decoupled audio projector on top of a self-supervised encoder to capture both global semantics and local details. The method also includes FineLAP-100k, a large-scale synthetic SED dataset created through a scalable curation pipeline to address temporal annotation scarcity.
AI.result: FineLAP achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple audio understanding tasks including retrieval, classification, sound event detection, and text-to-audio grounding. Ablation studies show that coarse- and fine-grained alignment are mutually beneficial.
AI.conclusion: FineLAP provides an effective training paradigm for advancing both clip- and frame-level alignment in audio-language models, demonstrating that heterogeneous data with varying granularity can be effectively leveraged to build better audio-language models.

title: VisG AV-HuBERT: Viseme-Guided AV-HuBERT
comment: Includes Supplementary Material. Accepted for Publication at International Conference on Pattern Recognition 2026 - ICPR 2026. Code is available at https://github.com/aristosp/visg_avhubert
summary: Audio-Visual Speech Recognition (AVSR) systems nowadays integrate Large Language Model (LLM) decoders with transformer-based encoders, achieving state-of-the-art results. However, the relative contributions of improved language modelling versus enhanced audiovisual encoding remain unclear. We propose Viseme-Guided AV-HuBERT (VisG AV-HuBERT), a multi-task fine-tuning framework that incorporates auxiliary viseme classification to strengthen the model's reliance on visual articulatory features. By extending AV-HuBERT with a lightweight viseme prediction sub-network, this method explicitly guides the encoder to preserve visual speech information. Evaluated on LRS3, VisG AV-HuBERT achieves comparable or improved performance over the baseline AV-HuBERT, with notable gains under heavy noise conditions. WER reduces from 13.59% to 6.60% (51.4% relative improvement) at -10 dB Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) for Speech noise. Deeper analysis reveals substantial reductions in substitution errors across noise types, demonstrating improved speech unit discrimination. Evaluation on LRS2 confirms generalization capability. Our results demonstrate that explicit viseme modelling enhances encoder representations, and provides a foundation for enhancing noise-robust AVSR through encoder-level improvements.

AI.tldr: VisG AV-HuBERT enhances AVSR by adding viseme classification to AV-HuBERT, improving noise robustness through better visual feature encoding rather than just language modeling.
AI.motivation: Current AVSR systems combine LLM decoders with transformer encoders, but it's unclear whether performance gains come from better language modeling or improved audiovisual encoding. The authors aim to strengthen the model's reliance on visual articulatory features through explicit viseme modeling.
AI.method: Proposes VisG AV-HuBERT, a multi-task fine-tuning framework that extends AV-HuBERT with a lightweight viseme prediction sub-network. This auxiliary viseme classification task explicitly guides the encoder to preserve visual speech information during training.
AI.result: On LRS3, achieves comparable or improved performance over baseline AV-HuBERT, with significant gains under heavy noise: WER reduces from 13.59% to 6.60% (51.4% relative improvement) at -10 dB SNR for speech noise. Shows substantial reduction in substitution errors across noise types, indicating improved speech unit discrimination. Generalizes well to LRS2.
AI.conclusion: Explicit viseme modeling enhances encoder representations and provides a foundation for improving noise-robust AVSR through encoder-level improvements rather than relying solely on decoder enhancements.

title: Temperature Control of Digital Glass Forming Processes
summary: Digital Glass Forming (DGF) is a new manufacturing process for low-batch glass fabrication. The work zone temperature in DGF processes must be maintained in the glass's working range to ensure good fabrication. If the temperature is too low, the filament will not wet to the substrate or previously deposited material and, if the temperature is too high, the filament may disengage from the substrate or previously deposited material, or it may partially vaporize. In this work, a real-time temperature control system capable of synchronizing process parameter, thermal camera, and visual camera data for the DGF process is introduced. A process parameter map for a scan velocity of 0.5 mm/s is constructed, as is a data-driven dynamic temperature process model. A digital controller is designed to regulate the work zone temperature. The temperature controller is a closed loop tracking controller that adjusts the commanded laser power to regulate the measured temperature. Two sets of experiments are conducted to analyze the controller performance. In the first set of experiments, single tracks on a substrate are fabricated with constant laser power and with the closed loop temperature controller. It is seen that the closed loop controller is able to extend the process parameter map into regions where using a constant laser power will result in a failed build. In the second set of experiments, walls are fabricated. Using constant laser power results in a failed build (i.e., material vaporization at the corners and the filament prematurely detaching from the substrate) as the temperature process dynamics change with layer and at the corners. The closed loop controller successfully fabricated the wall without vaporization at the corners and premature filament detachment as the controller adjusts the laser power to account for the changing temperature process dynamics.

AI.tldr: A real-time temperature control system for Digital Glass Forming (DGF) that uses closed-loop control to adjust laser power based on thermal measurements, enabling successful fabrication in challenging conditions where constant power fails.
AI.motivation: Temperature control is critical in DGF processes because improper temperatures cause fabrication failures - too low prevents proper wetting/adhesion, too high causes vaporization or detachment. Maintaining work zone temperature within the glass's working range is essential for successful fabrication.
AI.method: Developed a real-time temperature control system that synchronizes process parameters, thermal camera, and visual camera data. Created a process parameter map for 0.5 mm/s scan velocity and a data-driven dynamic temperature process model. Designed a digital closed-loop tracking controller that adjusts commanded laser power based on measured temperature feedback.
AI.result: The closed-loop controller extended the process parameter map into regions where constant laser power would fail. For single tracks, it enabled successful fabrication where constant power failed. For wall fabrication, it prevented vaporization at corners and premature filament detachment that occurred with constant power, successfully accounting for changing temperature dynamics with layer and geometry.
AI.conclusion: The closed-loop temperature control system successfully regulates work zone temperature in DGF processes, enabling fabrication in challenging conditions where open-loop constant power approaches fail, particularly addressing issues with changing thermal dynamics during layer-by-layer fabrication and at geometric features like corners.

title: Diff-VS: Efficient Audio-Aware Diffusion U-Net for Vocals Separation
summary: While diffusion models are best known for their performance in generative tasks, they have also been successfully applied to many other tasks, including audio source separation. However, current generative approaches to music source separation often underperform on standard objective metrics. In this paper, we address this issue by introducing a novel generative vocal separation model based on the Elucidated Diffusion Model (EDM) framework. Our model processes complex short-time Fourier transform spectrograms and employs an improved U-Net architecture based on music-informed design choices. Our approach matches discriminative baselines on objective metrics and achieves perceptual quality comparable to state-of-the-art systems, as assessed by proxy subjective metrics. We hope these results encourage broader exploration of generative methods for music source separation

AI.tldr: A generative vocal separation model using Elucidated Diffusion Model (EDM) framework achieves performance comparable to discriminative baselines on objective metrics and state-of-the-art perceptual quality.
AI.motivation: Current generative approaches to music source separation often underperform on standard objective metrics compared to discriminative methods, despite diffusion models' success in other domains including audio source separation.
AI.method: Novel generative vocal separation model based on Elucidated Diffusion Model (EDM) framework that processes complex short-time Fourier transform spectrograms and employs an improved U-Net architecture with music-informed design choices.
AI.result: The model matches discriminative baselines on objective metrics and achieves perceptual quality comparable to state-of-the-art systems as assessed by proxy subjective metrics.
AI.conclusion: These results demonstrate that generative methods can achieve competitive performance in music source separation and should encourage broader exploration of generative approaches in this domain.

title: Data-Driven Reachability of Nonlinear Lipschitz Systems via Koopman Operator Embeddings
summary: Data-driven safety verification of robotic systems often relies on zonotopic reachability analysis due to its scalability and computational efficiency. However, for nonlinear systems, these methods can become overly conservative, especially over long prediction horizons and under measurement noise. We propose a data-driven reachability framework based on the Koopman operator and zonotopic set representations that lifts the nonlinear system into a finite-dimensional, linear, state-input-dependent model. Reachable sets are then computed in the lifted space and projected back to the original state space to obtain guaranteed over-approximations of the true dynamics. The proposed method reduces conservatism while preserving formal safety guarantees, and we prove that the resulting reachable sets over-approximate the true reachable sets. Numerical simulations and real-world experiments on an autonomous vehicle show that the proposed approach yields substantially tighter reachable set over-approximations than both model-based and linear data-driven methods, particularly over long horizons.

AI.tldr: Data-driven reachability framework combining Koopman operator theory with zonotopic representations to reduce conservatism in safety verification of nonlinear robotic systems while preserving formal guarantees.
AI.motivation: Current data-driven safety verification methods using zonotopic reachability analysis become overly conservative for nonlinear systems, especially over long prediction horizons and under measurement noise, limiting their practical effectiveness.
AI.method: Proposes a data-driven reachability framework that lifts nonlinear systems into finite-dimensional, linear, state-input-dependent models using the Koopman operator, computes reachable sets in the lifted space using zonotopic representations, and projects them back to the original state space to obtain guaranteed over-approximations.
AI.result: The method reduces conservatism while preserving formal safety guarantees, with proofs showing the resulting reachable sets over-approximate the true reachable sets. Numerical simulations and real-world experiments on an autonomous vehicle demonstrate substantially tighter reachable set over-approximations than both model-based and linear data-driven methods, particularly over long horizons.
AI.conclusion: The Koopman-based zonotopic reachability framework effectively addresses the conservatism problem in data-driven safety verification for nonlinear robotic systems, providing tighter over-approximations while maintaining formal guarantees, making it particularly suitable for long-horizon predictions in practical applications like autonomous vehicles.

title: Advanced Capacity Accreditation of Future Energy System Resources with Deep Uncertainties
comment: 10 pages, 10 figures. Prepared for submission to an IEEE Transactions journal
summary: The electric power sector has seen an increased penetration of renewable energy sources (RESs) that could strain the system reliability due to their inherent uncertainties in availability and controllability. Effective load carrying capability (ELCC) is widely used to quantify the reliability contributions of these RESs. However, existing ELCC methods can over- or under-estimate their contributions and often neglect or simplify other critical factors such as transmission constraints and evolving climate trends, leading to inaccurate capacity credit (CC) allocations and inefficient reliability procurement in capacity markets. To address these limitations, this paper proposes TRACED (TRansmission And Climate Enhanced Delta) -- an advanced capacity accreditation approach that integrates transmission constraints and climate-adjusted system conditions into a Delta ELCC evaluation. Case studies on a modified IEEE-118 bus system with high RES and energy storage penetrations demonstrate that TRACED produces portfolio-consistent CC allocations by capturing resource interactions and avoiding the double-counting of shared reliability benefits inherent in marginal ELCC, which may otherwise lead to under-procurement of reliability resources. Results further demonstrate that transmission congestion and evolving climate trends have mutual impacts on CC allocation, justifying their necessary integration into TRACED.

AI.tldr: TRACED is a new capacity accreditation method that integrates transmission constraints and climate-adjusted conditions into Delta ELCC evaluation to improve reliability resource allocation in power systems with high renewable penetration.
AI.motivation: Existing ELCC methods for renewable energy sources have limitations: they can over- or under-estimate reliability contributions, often neglect transmission constraints and evolving climate trends, leading to inaccurate capacity credit allocations and inefficient reliability procurement in capacity markets.
AI.method: Proposes TRACED (TRansmission And Climate Enhanced Delta) - an advanced capacity accreditation approach that integrates transmission constraints and climate-adjusted system conditions into a Delta ELCC evaluation framework.
AI.result: Case studies on a modified IEEE-118 bus system with high RES and energy storage penetrations show that TRACED produces portfolio-consistent capacity credit allocations by capturing resource interactions and avoiding double-counting of shared reliability benefits. Results demonstrate that transmission congestion and evolving climate trends have mutual impacts on capacity credit allocation.
AI.conclusion: TRACED addresses limitations of existing ELCC methods by properly integrating transmission constraints and climate trends, leading to more accurate capacity credit allocations and avoiding under-procurement of reliability resources in capacity markets.

title: Finite-Time Analysis of Projected Two-Time-Scale Stochastic Approximation
summary: We study the finite-time convergence of projected linear two-time-scale stochastic approximation with constant step sizes and Polyak--Ruppert averaging. We establish an explicit mean-square error bound, decomposing it into two interpretable components, an approximation error determined by the constrained subspace and a statistical error decaying at a sublinear rate, with constants expressed through restricted stability margins and a coupling invertibility condition. These constants cleanly separate the effect of subspace choice (approximation errors) from the effect of the averaging horizon (statistical errors). We illustrate our theoretical results through a number of numerical experiments on both synthetic and reinforcement learning problems.

AI.tldr: Analysis of finite-time convergence for projected linear two-time-scale stochastic approximation with constant step sizes and Polyak-Ruppert averaging, providing explicit mean-square error bounds with interpretable components.
AI.motivation: To understand the finite-time convergence properties of projected linear two-time-scale stochastic approximation algorithms with constant step sizes, which are widely used in reinforcement learning and optimization but lack comprehensive finite-time analysis with clear error decomposition.
AI.method: Projected linear two-time-scale stochastic approximation with constant step sizes and Polyak-Ruppert averaging, analyzed through mean-square error bounds decomposed into approximation error (determined by constrained subspace) and statistical error (decaying sublinearly).
AI.result: Established explicit mean-square error bound with two interpretable components: approximation error from constrained subspace and statistical error decaying at sublinear rate, with constants expressed through restricted stability margins and coupling invertibility condition.
AI.conclusion: The analysis provides clean separation between subspace choice effects (approximation errors) and averaging horizon effects (statistical errors), with theoretical results validated through numerical experiments on synthetic and reinforcement learning problems.

title: Agentic AI and Occupational Displacement: A Multi-Regional Task Exposure Analysis of Emerging Labor Market Disruption
comment: 26 pages, 2 figures, 6 tables. Submitted to IMF-OECD-PIIE-World Bank Conference on Labor Markets and Structural Transformation 2026
summary: This paper extends the Acemoglu-Restrepo task exposure framework to address the labor market effects of agentic artificial intelligence systems: autonomous AI agents capable of completing entire occupational workflows rather than discrete tasks. Unlike prior automation technologies that substitute for individual subtasks, agentic AI systems execute end-to-end workflows involving multi-step reasoning, tool invocation, and autonomous decision-making, substantially expanding occupational displacement risk beyond what existing task-level analyses capture. We introduce the Agentic Task Exposure (ATE) score, a composite measure computed algorithmically from O*NET task data using calibrated adoption parameters--not a regression estimate--incorporating AI capability scores, workflow coverage factors, and logistic adoption velocity. Applying the ATE framework across five major US technology regions (Seattle-Tacoma, San Francisco Bay Area, Austin, New York, and Boston) over a 2025-2030 horizon, we find that 93.2% of the 236 analyzed occupations across six information-intensive SOC groups (financial, legal, healthcare, healthcare support, sales, and administrative/clerical) cross the moderate-risk threshold (ATE >= 0.35) in Tier 1 regions by 2030, with credit analysts, judges, and sustainability specialists reaching ATE scores of 0.43-0.47. We simultaneously identify seventeen emerging occupational categories benefiting from reinstatement effects, concentrated in human-AI collaboration, AI governance, and domain-specific AI operations roles. Our findings carry implications for workforce transition policy, regional economic planning, and the temporal dynamics of labor market adjustment

AI.tldr: This paper extends task exposure analysis to agentic AI systems that can complete entire workflows, introducing an Agentic Task Exposure (ATE) score that reveals 93.2% of analyzed occupations face moderate displacement risk by 2030 in major US tech regions, while identifying 17 emerging occupational categories benefiting from AI collaboration.
AI.motivation: Traditional task exposure frameworks (like Acemoglu-Restrepo) analyze automation at the discrete task level, but agentic AI systems can execute complete occupational workflows involving multi-step reasoning and autonomous decision-making. This creates substantially different displacement risks that existing task-level analyses fail to capture, necessitating a new analytical framework.
AI.method: The paper introduces the Agentic Task Exposure (ATE) score, a composite measure computed algorithmically from O*NET task data using calibrated adoption parameters (not regression estimates). The ATE incorporates AI capability scores, workflow coverage factors, and logistic adoption velocity. The framework is applied across five major US technology regions (Seattle-Tacoma, San Francisco Bay Area, Austin, New York, and Boston) over 2025-2030, analyzing 236 occupations across six information-intensive SOC groups.
AI.result: 93.2% of the 236 analyzed occupations across financial, legal, healthcare, healthcare support, sales, and administrative/clerical groups cross the moderate-risk threshold (ATE ≥ 0.35) in Tier 1 regions by 2030. Credit analysts, judges, and sustainability specialists reach the highest ATE scores (0.43-0.47). Simultaneously, seventeen emerging occupational categories benefit from reinstatement effects, concentrated in human-AI collaboration, AI governance, and domain-specific AI operations roles.
AI.conclusion: Agentic AI systems fundamentally change labor market displacement dynamics by automating entire workflows rather than discrete tasks, creating substantially higher occupational displacement risks than previously estimated. The findings have significant implications for workforce transition policy, regional economic planning, and understanding the temporal dynamics of labor market adjustment to AI-driven automation.

title: Scalable machine learning-based approaches for energy saving in densely deployed Open RAN
summary: Densely deployed base stations are responsible for the majority of the energy consumed in Radio access network (RAN). While these deployments are crucial to deliver the required data rate in busy hours of the day, the network can save energy by switching some of them to sleep mode and maintain the coverage and quality of service with the other ones. Benefiting from the flexibility provided by the Open RAN in embedding machine learning (ML) in network operations, in this work we propose Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based energy saving solutions. Firstly we propose 3 different DRL-based methods in the form of xApps which control the Active/Sleep mode of up to 6 radio units (RUs) from Near Real time RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC). We also propose a further scalable federated DRL-based solution with an aggregator as an rApp in None Real time RIC and local agents as xApps. Our simulation results present the convergence of the proposed methods. We also compare the performance of our federated DRL across three layouts spanning 6--24 RUs and 500--1000\,m regions, including a composite multi-region scenario. The results show that our proposed federated TD3 algorithm achieves up to 43.75\% faster convergence, more than 50\% network energy saving and 37. 4\% lower training energy versus centralized baselines, while maintaining the quality of service and improving the robustness of the policy.

AI.tldr: Proposes DRL-based energy saving solutions for Open RAN using xApps/rApps to control RU sleep modes, with federated DRL achieving faster convergence and significant energy savings.
AI.motivation: Densely deployed base stations consume most RAN energy; networks can save energy by switching some RUs to sleep mode while maintaining coverage and QoS, leveraging Open RAN's flexibility for ML integration.
AI.method: Proposes 3 DRL-based methods as xApps controlling Active/Sleep modes of up to 6 RUs from Near-RT RIC, plus a scalable federated DRL solution with aggregator rApp in Non-RT RIC and local agent xApps.
AI.result: Federated TD3 achieves up to 43.75% faster convergence, >50% network energy saving, 37.4% lower training energy vs centralized baselines, while maintaining QoS and improving policy robustness across 6-24 RU layouts.
AI.conclusion: DRL-based energy saving solutions effectively reduce RAN energy consumption; federated DRL approach offers superior scalability, convergence speed, and energy efficiency while maintaining service quality.

title: Agentic AI for Clinical Urgency Mapping and Queue Optimization in High-Volume Outpatient Departments: A Simulation-Based Evaluation
comment: 17 pages, 3 figures, 7 tables. Code available at https://github.com/ravyg/opd-agentic-ai-triage
summary: Outpatient departments (OPDs) in Indian public hospitals face severe overcrowding, with daily volumes reaching 200--8,000 patients~\cite{aiims2020annual}. The prevailing First-Come-First-Served (FCFS) token system treats all patients equally regardless of clinical urgency, leading to dangerous delays for critical cases. We present an agentic AI framework integrating six components: voice-based multilingual symptom capture (modeled), LLM-powered severity prediction, load-aware physician assignment, adaptive queue optimization with urgency drift detection, a multi-objective orchestrator, and a Patient Memory System for longitudinal context-aware triage. Evaluated through discrete-event simulation of a District Hospital in Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh) with 368 synthetic patients over 30 runs, the framework achieves 94.2\% critical patients seen within 10 minutes (vs.~30.8\% under FCFS), detects $\sim$236 simulated urgency drift events per session (modeled via stochastic deterioration probabilities), identifies $\sim$11.9 additional hidden-critical cases via patient memory, and recomposes queue urgency distribution from 13/36/158/161 (Critical/High/Medium/Low) to $\sim$25/178/115/50 through continuous reassessment, while maintaining comparable throughput ($\sim$40.4 patients/hour).

AI.tldr: An AI framework for Indian hospital OPDs that replaces FCFS with voice-based multilingual symptom capture, LLM severity prediction, and adaptive queue optimization to prioritize critical patients while maintaining throughput.
AI.motivation: Indian public hospital OPDs face severe overcrowding (200-8,000 patients daily) with FCFS systems that treat all patients equally regardless of clinical urgency, causing dangerous delays for critical cases.
AI.method: Agentic AI framework with six components: 1) voice-based multilingual symptom capture, 2) LLM-powered severity prediction, 3) load-aware physician assignment, 4) adaptive queue optimization with urgency drift detection, 5) multi-objective orchestrator, and 6) Patient Memory System for longitudinal context-aware triage.
AI.result: Simulation with 368 synthetic patients over 30 runs shows: 94.2% critical patients seen within 10 minutes (vs. 30.8% under FCFS), detects ~236 urgency drift events per session, identifies ~11.9 additional hidden-critical cases via patient memory, recomposes queue urgency distribution from 13/36/158/161 (Critical/High/Medium/Low) to ~25/178/115/50, while maintaining comparable throughput (~40.4 patients/hour).
AI.conclusion: The AI framework significantly improves critical patient prioritization and safety in overcrowded Indian OPDs while maintaining operational efficiency, demonstrating the potential of agentic AI systems for healthcare queue management.

title: Dissipation-assisted stabilization of periodic orbits via actuated exterior impacts in hybrid mechanical systems with symmetry
summary: Impulsive mechanical systems exhibit discontinuous jumps in their state, and when such jumps are triggered by spatial events, the geometry of the impact surface carries information about the controllability of the hybrid dynamics. For mechanical systems defined on principal $G$-bundles, two qualitatively distinct types of impacts arise: interior impacts, associated with events on the shape space, and exterior impacts, associated with events on the fibers. A key distinction is that interior impacts preserve the mechanical connection, whereas exterior impacts generally do not. In this paper, we exploit this distinction by allowing actuation through exterior impacts. We study the pendulum-on-a-cart system, derive controlled reset laws induced by moving-wall impacts, and analyze the resulting periodic motions. Our results show that reset action alone does not provide a convincing stabilizing regime, whereas the addition of dissipation in the continuous flow yields exponentially stable periodic behavior for suitable feedback gains.

AI.tldr: Exterior impacts (fiber-triggered) can be used for actuation in mechanical systems on principal bundles, unlike interior impacts that preserve mechanical connection. Applied to pendulum-on-cart with moving-wall impacts, reset action alone insufficient for stabilization, but combined with continuous dissipation yields exponentially stable periodic motions.
AI.motivation: For mechanical systems on principal G-bundles, exterior impacts (fiber-triggered) don't preserve the mechanical connection, unlike interior impacts. This distinction enables using exterior impacts for actuation, exploring how impact geometry affects controllability in hybrid dynamical systems.
AI.method: Study pendulum-on-cart system with moving-wall impacts, derive controlled reset laws from exterior impacts, analyze resulting periodic motions. Compare stabilization regimes: reset action alone vs. reset action combined with dissipation in continuous flow.
AI.result: Reset action alone doesn't provide convincing stabilization. However, adding dissipation in the continuous flow yields exponentially stable periodic behavior for suitable feedback gains, demonstrating effective hybrid control strategy.
AI.conclusion: Exterior impacts offer viable actuation mechanism for mechanical systems on principal bundles. Effective stabilization requires combining impact-based reset actions with continuous dissipation, enabling exponentially stable periodic motions through hybrid control design.

title: Hybrid Energy-Based Models for Physical AI: Provably Stable Identification of Port-Hamiltonian Dynamics
summary: Energy-based models (EBMs) implement inference as gradient descent on a learned Lyapunov function, yielding interpretable, structure-preserving alternatives to black-box neural ODEs and aligning naturally with physical AI. Yet their use in system identification remains limited, and existing architectures lack formal stability guarantees that globally preclude unstable modes. We address this gap by introducing an EBM framework for system identification with stable, dissipative, absorbing invariant dynamics. Unlike classical global Lyapunov stability, absorbing invariance expands the class of stability-preserving architectures, enabling more flexible and expressive EBMs. We extend EBM theory to nonsmooth activations by establishing negative energy dissipation via Clarke derivatives and deriving new conditions for radial unboundedness, exposing a stability-expressivity tradeoff in standard EBMs. To overcome this, we introduce a hybrid architecture with a dynamical visible layer and static hidden layers, prove absorbing invariance under mild assumptions, and show that these guarantees extend to port-Hamiltonian EBMs. Experiments on metric-deformed multi-well and ring systems validate the approach, showcasing how our hybrid EBM architecture combines expressivity with sound and provable safety guarantees by design.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a hybrid energy-based model framework for system identification with formal stability guarantees, overcoming limitations of existing EBMs that lack global stability assurances while maintaining expressivity.
AI.motivation: EBMs offer interpretable, structure-preserving alternatives to black-box neural ODEs and align naturally with physical AI, but their use in system identification remains limited due to lack of formal stability guarantees that globally preclude unstable modes.
AI.method: The authors extend EBM theory to nonsmooth activations using Clarke derivatives, derive conditions for radial unboundedness, and introduce a hybrid architecture with dynamical visible layer and static hidden layers that ensures absorbing invariance under mild assumptions. They also extend these guarantees to port-Hamiltonian EBMs.
AI.result: Experiments on metric-deformed multi-well and ring systems validate the approach, demonstrating that the hybrid EBM architecture combines expressivity with provable safety guarantees by design.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework addresses the stability-expressivity tradeoff in standard EBMs by introducing absorbing invariance (a broader stability concept than classical global Lyapunov stability), enabling more flexible and expressive EBMs with formal stability guarantees for system identification.

title: Data-Driven Reachability Analysis via Diffusion Models with PAC Guarantees
comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, submitted to the 65th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC 2026)
summary: We present a data-driven framework for reachability analysis of nonlinear dynamical systems that requires no explicit model. A denoising diffusion probabilistic model learns the time-evolving state distribution of a dynamical system from trajectory data alone. The predicted reachable set takes the form of a sublevel set of a nonconformity score derived from the reconstruction error, with the threshold calibrated via the Learn Then Test procedure so that the probability of excluding a reachable state is bounded with high probability. Experiments on three nonlinear systems, a forced Duffing oscillator, a planar quadrotor, and a high-dimensional reaction-diffusion system, confirm that the empirical miss rate remains below the Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) bound while scaling to state dimensions beyond the reach of classical grid-based and polynomial methods.

AI.tldr: Data-driven reachability analysis using diffusion models learns system dynamics from trajectory data without explicit models, providing PAC-guaranteed reachable sets via calibrated reconstruction error thresholds.
AI.motivation: Classical reachability analysis methods for nonlinear dynamical systems often require explicit system models and face scalability issues with high-dimensional states. There's a need for model-free approaches that can handle complex systems while providing formal guarantees.
AI.method: Uses denoising diffusion probabilistic models to learn time-evolving state distributions from trajectory data. Derives reachable sets as sublevel sets of a nonconformity score based on reconstruction error. Calibrates thresholds using the Learn Then Test procedure to provide PAC guarantees on coverage probability.
AI.result: Empirical validation on three nonlinear systems (forced Duffing oscillator, planar quadrotor, high-dimensional reaction-diffusion system) shows the method maintains miss rates below the PAC bound while scaling to state dimensions beyond classical grid-based and polynomial methods.
AI.conclusion: The framework enables model-free reachability analysis with formal guarantees, successfully handling high-dimensional nonlinear systems that challenge traditional methods, demonstrating practical scalability and reliability.

title: Certified Set Convergence for Piecewise Affine Systems via Neural Lyapunov Functions
comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to the 65th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC 2026)
summary: Safety-critical control of piecewise affine (PWA) systems under bounded additive disturbances requires guarantees not for individual states but for entire state sets simultaneously: a single control action must steer every state in the set toward a target, even as sets crossing mode boundaries split and evolve under distinct affine dynamics. Certifying such set convergence via neural Lyapunov functions couples the Lipschitz constants of the value function and the policy, yet certified bounds for expressive networks exceed true values by orders of magnitude, creating a certification barrier. We resolve this through a three-stage pipeline that decouples verification from the policy. A value function from Hamilton-Jacobi backward reachability, trained via reinforcement learning, is the Lyapunov candidate. A permutation-invariant Deep Sets controller, distilled via regret minimization, produces a common action. Verification propagates zonotopes through the value network, yielding verified Lyapunov upper bounds over entire sets without bounding the policy Lipschitz constant. On four benchmarks up to dimension six, including systems with per-mode operator norms exceeding unity, the framework certifies set convergence with positive margin on every system. A spectrally constrained local certificate completes the terminal guarantee, and the set-actor is the only tested method to achieve full strict set containment, at constant-time online cost.

AI.tldr: A three-stage pipeline for certifying safety-critical control of piecewise affine systems under disturbances by decoupling verification from policy, using Hamilton-Jacobi reachability for value functions, Deep Sets for controllers, and zonotope propagation for verification without bounding policy Lipschitz constants.
AI.motivation: Safety-critical control of piecewise affine systems under bounded disturbances requires set-based guarantees where a single control action must steer entire state sets toward targets, even when sets split across mode boundaries. Existing neural Lyapunov approaches couple value function and policy Lipschitz constants, but certified bounds for expressive networks exceed true values by orders of magnitude, creating a certification barrier.
AI.method: Three-stage pipeline: 1) Value function from Hamilton-Jacobi backward reachability trained via reinforcement learning as Lyapunov candidate, 2) Permutation-invariant Deep Sets controller distilled via regret minimization to produce common actions, 3) Verification via zonotope propagation through value network yielding verified Lyapunov upper bounds over entire sets without bounding policy Lipschitz constant.
AI.result: On four benchmarks up to dimension six, including systems with per-mode operator norms exceeding unity, the framework certifies set convergence with positive margin on every system. The set-actor achieves full strict set containment at constant-time online cost, and a spectrally constrained local certificate provides terminal guarantee.
AI.conclusion: The proposed pipeline successfully decouples verification from policy, overcoming the certification barrier by avoiding bounding of policy Lipschitz constants. The approach enables certified set convergence for piecewise affine systems under disturbances with positive margins and achieves strict set containment with efficient online computation.

title: From Net Load Modifiers to Firm Capacity: The Role of Distributed Energy Resources in Resource Adequacy
summary: Distributed energy resources (DERs) such as rooftop solar, battery storage, and demand response offer substantial potential for power system reliability, yet integrating them into resource adequacy (RA) frameworks as firm capacity contributors remains difficult across jurisdictions. Existing analyses often treat these barriers as isolated technical problems at individual stages of the RA participation process, overlooking the cross-stage dependencies that prevent reforms at one stage from producing scalable participation. This paper introduces a four-gate compliance pathway (entry and classification, metering and verification, accreditation, and enforcement), preceded by an upstream forecasting layer, as a unified lens for tracing where DER capacity value is lost at the institutional interfaces between these stages. Using a document-grounded comparative synthesis of tariff provisions, compliance protocols, and regulatory documents across five jurisdictions spanning U.S. capacity markets and European capacity remuneration mechanisms, we show that these barriers persist despite substantial variation in market design and regulatory structure, indicating that the problem is structural rather than jurisdiction-specific. We identify three cross-stage coupling mechanisms that explain why gate-level reforms have repeatedly failed to scale DER participation, and derive coordination principles for end-to-end compliance redesign. The central finding is that compliance architecture, rather than DER technology itself, is the binding constraint on translating DER capability into firm RA contributions.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes structural barriers preventing distributed energy resources (DERs) from contributing to resource adequacy frameworks, identifying cross-stage dependencies in compliance pathways as the key constraint rather than technical limitations.
AI.motivation: Distributed energy resources (DERs) offer substantial potential for power system reliability but face persistent barriers to integration as firm capacity contributors in resource adequacy frameworks across jurisdictions, with existing analyses treating these as isolated technical problems rather than structural issues.
AI.method: Introduces a four-gate compliance pathway (entry/classification, metering/verification, accreditation, enforcement) with upstream forecasting layer as analytical framework; uses document-grounded comparative synthesis of tariff provisions, compliance protocols, and regulatory documents across five jurisdictions spanning U.S. capacity markets and European capacity remuneration mechanisms.
AI.result: Identifies three cross-stage coupling mechanisms explaining why gate-level reforms fail to scale DER participation; shows barriers persist despite substantial variation in market design and regulatory structure, indicating structural rather than jurisdiction-specific problem; finds compliance architecture is the binding constraint on translating DER capability into firm resource adequacy contributions.
AI.conclusion: The central finding is that compliance architecture, rather than DER technology itself, is the binding constraint on translating DER capability into firm resource adequacy contributions, requiring coordination principles for end-to-end compliance redesign rather than isolated gate-level reforms.

title: Set-Based Value Function Characterization and Neural Approximation of Stabilization Domains for Input-Constrained Discrete-Time Systems
summary: Analyzing nonlinear systems with stabilizable controlled invariant sets (CISs) requires accurate estimation of their domains of stabilization (DOS) together with associated stabilizing controllers. Despite extensive research, estimating DOSs for general nonlinear systems remains challenging due to fundamental theoretical and computational limitations. In this paper, we propose a novel framework for estimating DOSs for controlled input-constrained discrete-time systems. The DOS is characterized via newly introduced value functions defined on metric spaces of compact sets. We establish the fundamental properties of these value functions and derive the associated Bellman-type (Zubov-type) functional equations. Building on this characterization, we develop a physics-informed neural network (NN) framework that learns the value functions by embedding the derived functional equations directly into the training process. The proposed methodology is demonstrated through two numerical examples, illustrating its ability to accurately estimate DOSs and synthesize stabilizing controllers from the learned value functions.

AI.tldr: A novel physics-informed neural network framework for estimating domains of stabilization and synthesizing controllers for input-constrained discrete-time nonlinear systems.
AI.motivation: Accurate estimation of domains of stabilization for nonlinear systems with stabilizable controlled invariant sets remains challenging due to theoretical and computational limitations, despite extensive research.
AI.method: Characterizes DOS via value functions on metric spaces of compact sets, establishes their properties and Bellman-type functional equations, then develops physics-informed neural networks that embed these equations into training.
AI.result: Demonstrated through two numerical examples showing accurate DOS estimation and successful synthesis of stabilizing controllers from learned value functions.
AI.conclusion: Proposed framework effectively addresses DOS estimation challenges for input-constrained discrete-time nonlinear systems by combining theoretical characterization with physics-informed neural network learning.

title: Nonlinear Moving-Horizon Estimation Using State- and Control-Dependent Models
summary: This paper presents a state- and control-dependent moving-horizon estimation (SCD-MHE) algorithm for nonlinear discrete-time systems. Within this framework, a pseudo-linear representation of nonlinear dynamics is leveraged utilizing state- and control-dependent coefficients, where the solution to a moving-horizon estimation problem is iteratively refined. At each discrete time step, a quadratic program is executed over a sliding window of historical measurements. Moreover, system matrices are consecutively updated based upon prior iterates to capture nonlinear regimes. In contrast to the extended Kalman filter (EKF) and the unscented Kalman filter (UKF), nonlinearities and bounds are accommodated within a structured optimization framework, thereby circumventing the reliance on local Jacobian matrices. Furthermore, theoretical analysis is presented to establish the convergence of the iterative sequence, and bounded estimation errors are mathematically guaranteed under uniform observability conditions. Finally, comparative numerical experiments utilizing a quadrotor vertical kinematics system demonstrate that the SCD-MHE achieves superior estimation accuracy relative to the EKF, the UKF, and a fully nonlinear moving-horizon estimator, while reducing per-step computational latency by over an order of magnitude.

AI.tldr: SCD-MHE is a moving-horizon estimation algorithm for nonlinear systems that uses state- and control-dependent coefficients in a pseudo-linear representation, solved iteratively via quadratic programming, offering improved accuracy over EKF/UKF with reduced computational cost.
AI.motivation: Existing nonlinear estimation methods like EKF and UKF have limitations: EKF relies on local Jacobian linearization which can be inaccurate, while UKF uses sigma-point approximations. Both struggle with constraints and lack structured optimization frameworks. There's a need for estimators that handle nonlinearities and constraints more effectively while maintaining computational efficiency.
AI.method: SCD-MHE uses a pseudo-linear representation of nonlinear dynamics with state- and control-dependent coefficients. At each time step, it solves a quadratic program over a sliding window of measurements. System matrices are iteratively updated based on prior estimates to capture nonlinear behavior. The approach avoids Jacobian computations and handles constraints within an optimization framework.
AI.result: Theoretical analysis proves convergence of the iterative sequence and mathematically guarantees bounded estimation errors under uniform observability conditions. Numerical experiments on a quadrotor vertical kinematics system show SCD-MHE achieves superior estimation accuracy compared to EKF, UKF, and fully nonlinear MHE, while reducing per-step computational latency by over an order of magnitude.
AI.conclusion: SCD-MHE provides an effective framework for nonlinear estimation that combines the benefits of moving-horizon optimization with computational efficiency. It outperforms traditional nonlinear filters in accuracy while being significantly faster than fully nonlinear MHE, making it suitable for real-time applications with nonlinear dynamics and constraints.

title: Phase Relationship between Spinal Motion and Limb Support Determines High-speed Running Performance in a Cheetah Model with Asymmetric Spinal Stiffness
summary: Cheetahs are characterized by large spinal flexion and extension during high-speed running, yet the dynamical role of the phase relationship between spinal motion and limb support remains unclear. We aimed to clarify how this phase relationship affects running performance, focusing on the effect of asymmetric spinal stiffness. Using a simple planar cheetah model with asymmetric torsional spinal stiffness, we numerically searched for periodic bounding solutions over a range of stiffness parameters and compared their ground reaction forces, horizontal velocities, and stability. We obtained both cheetah-like solutions, in which the spine extends after hindlimb liftoff and flexes after forelimb liftoff, and non-cheetah-like solutions, in which the spine flexes after hindlimb liftoff and extends after forelimb liftoff. Under asymmetric spinal stiffness, cheetah-like solutions reduced ground reaction forces while maintaining horizontal velocity more effectively than non-cheetah-like solutions. The phase relationship between spinal motion and stance timing is a key determinant of high-speed running performance. These findings provide a dynamical understanding of cheetah locomotion and suggest design principles for spined legged robots.

AI.tldr: Cheetah-like spinal motion phase (extension after hindlimb liftoff, flexion after forelimb liftoff) with asymmetric stiffness reduces ground reaction forces while maintaining speed, optimizing high-speed running performance.
AI.motivation: To understand the dynamical role of spinal motion phase relationship with limb support in cheetah high-speed running, particularly how asymmetric spinal stiffness affects running performance.
AI.method: Used a simple planar cheetah model with asymmetric torsional spinal stiffness, numerically searched for periodic bounding solutions across stiffness parameters, comparing ground reaction forces, horizontal velocities, and stability.
AI.result: Found both cheetah-like solutions (spine extends after hindlimb liftoff, flexes after forelimb liftoff) and non-cheetah-like solutions (opposite phase). Cheetah-like solutions with asymmetric stiffness reduced ground reaction forces while maintaining horizontal velocity more effectively.
AI.conclusion: The phase relationship between spinal motion and stance timing is crucial for high-speed running performance. These findings provide dynamical understanding of cheetah locomotion and suggest design principles for spined legged robots.

title: Event-Triggered Adaptive Taylor-Lagrange Control for Safety-Critical Systems
summary: This paper studies safety-critical control for nonlinear systems under sampled-data implementations of the controller. The recently proposed Taylor--Lagrange Control (TLC) method provides rigorous safety guarantees but relies on a fixed discretization-related parameter, which can lead to infeasibility or unsafety in the presence of input constraints and inter-sampling effects. To address these limitations, we propose an adaptive Taylor--Lagrange Control (aTLC) framework with an event-triggered implementation, where the discretization-related parameter defines the discretization time scale and is selected online as state-dependent rather than fixed. This enables the controller to dynamically balance feasibility and safety by adjusting the effective time scale of the Taylor expansion. The resulting controller is implemented as a sequence of Quadratic Programs (QPs) with input constraints. We further introduce a selection rule to choose the discretization-related parameter from a finite candidate set, favoring feasible inputs and improved safety. Simulation results on an adaptive cruise control (ACC) problem demonstrate that the proposed approach improves feasibility, guarantees safety, and achieves smoother control actions compared to TLC while requiring a single automatically tuned parameter.

AI.tldr: Adaptive Taylor-Lagrange Control (aTLC) with event-triggered implementation improves safety-critical control for nonlinear systems under sampled-data control by dynamically adjusting discretization time scales to balance feasibility and safety.
AI.motivation: The existing Taylor-Lagrange Control (TLC) method provides safety guarantees but uses a fixed discretization parameter that can cause infeasibility or unsafety when dealing with input constraints and inter-sampling effects in sampled-data control implementations.
AI.method: Proposes adaptive Taylor-Lagrange Control (aTLC) with event-triggered implementation where the discretization parameter becomes state-dependent and is selected online. The controller is implemented as a sequence of Quadratic Programs (QPs) with input constraints, and includes a selection rule to choose the discretization parameter from a finite candidate set to favor feasible inputs and improved safety.
AI.result: Simulation results on an adaptive cruise control (ACC) problem demonstrate improved feasibility, guaranteed safety, smoother control actions compared to TLC, while requiring only a single automatically tuned parameter.
AI.conclusion: The aTLC framework successfully addresses limitations of fixed-parameter TLC by enabling dynamic adjustment of discretization time scales, providing better balance between feasibility and safety in safety-critical control for nonlinear systems under sampled-data implementations.

title: Willems' Fundamental Lemma with Large Noisy Fragmented Dataset
summary: Willems' Fundamental Lemma enables parameterizing all trajectories generated by a Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) system directly from data. However, this lemma relies on the assumption of noiseless measurements. In this paper, we provide an approach that enables the applicability of Willems' Fundamental Lemma with a large noisy-input, noisy-output fragmented dataset, without requiring prior knowledge of the noise distribution. We introduce a computationally tractable and lightweight algorithm that, despite processing a large dataset, executes in the order of seconds to estimate the invariants of the underlying system, which is obscured by noise. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

AI.tldr: A computationally efficient algorithm that enables Willems' Fundamental Lemma to work with noisy, fragmented datasets without requiring noise distribution knowledge.
AI.motivation: Willems' Fundamental Lemma requires noiseless measurements, limiting its practical application to real-world scenarios where data is noisy and fragmented.
AI.method: Introduces a computationally tractable, lightweight algorithm that processes large noisy-input, noisy-output fragmented datasets to estimate system invariants obscured by noise, without requiring prior noise distribution knowledge.
AI.result: The algorithm executes in seconds despite processing large datasets, and simulation results demonstrate its effectiveness in enabling Willems' Fundamental Lemma with noisy data.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method successfully extends Willems' Fundamental Lemma to practical scenarios with noisy, fragmented datasets, making data-driven system identification more applicable to real-world systems.

title: Demand response potential evaluation of a zero carbon hydrogen metallurgy system considering shaft furnace's flexibility
summary: The increasing penetration of intermittent renewable energy sources and the retirement of thermal units have widened the power system flexibility gap. Industrial demand response (DR) driven by real-time pricing is widely regarded as a viable solution. In this paper, we propose a framework to quantify the DR potential of a zero-carbon hydrogen metallurgy system (ZCHMS) considering shaft furnace's flexibility. First, we model the shaft furnace as a constrained flexible load and validate the model via simulation, achieving a root mean square error of 4.48\% of the rated load. Second, we formulate a DR potential evaluation method that determines baseline and DR-based production scheduling schemes by minimizing operating cost subject to production orders. Finally, the numerical results show that compared with the baseline, DR-based ZCHMS reduces operating cost by 6.6\%, incentivizing demand-side management in ironmaking and strengthening power-ironmaking synergies.

AI.tldr: A framework to quantify demand response potential of zero-carbon hydrogen metallurgy systems by modeling shaft furnace flexibility and optimizing production scheduling to reduce operating costs.
AI.motivation: The increasing penetration of intermittent renewable energy sources and retirement of thermal units have created a power system flexibility gap, requiring industrial demand response solutions to maintain grid stability.
AI.method: 1) Model the shaft furnace as a constrained flexible load and validate via simulation; 2) Formulate a DR potential evaluation method that determines baseline and DR-based production scheduling schemes by minimizing operating cost subject to production orders.
AI.result: The shaft furnace model achieved a root mean square error of 4.48% of rated load. DR-based ZCHMS reduces operating cost by 6.6% compared to baseline, demonstrating significant economic benefits for demand-side management in ironmaking.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework successfully quantifies DR potential in zero-carbon hydrogen metallurgy systems, incentivizing demand-side management in ironmaking and strengthening power-ironmaking synergies to address power system flexibility challenges.

title: Data-Attributed Adaptive Control Barrier Functions: Safety-Certified Training Data Curation via Influence Analysis
summary: Learning-based adaptation of Control Barrier Function (CBF) parameters offers a promising path toward safe autonomous navigation that balances conservatism with performance. Yet the accuracy of the underlying safety predictor is ultimately constrained by training data quality, and no prior work has formally characterized how prediction errors propagate through the adaptive pipeline to degrade closed-loop safety guarantees. We introduce Data-Attributed Adaptive CBF (DA-CBF), a framework that integrates TracIn-based data attribution into adaptive CBF learning. Our theoretical contributions are fourfold: (i) corrected two-sided bounds relating the safety-loss surrogate to the CBF constraint margin; (ii) a safety margin preservation theorem showing that prediction error induces quantifiable margin degradation and, via a smooth parameter selector, yields a genuine closed-loop forward invariance guarantee not conditioned on a fixed trajectory; (iii) a CBF-QP constraint perturbation bound that links prediction accuracy directly to recursive feasibility; and (iv) a principled leave-one-out justification for influence-based data curation under explicit smoothness assumptions. On a DynamicUnicycle2D benchmark, DA-CBF reduces prediction RMSE by 35.6\%, expands the certified safe operating set by 39\%, and achieves collision-free navigation in a 16-obstacle environment where the uncurated baseline incurs 3 collisions.

AI.tldr: DA-CBF integrates data attribution into adaptive CBF learning to quantify how prediction errors affect safety guarantees, providing theoretical bounds and improved performance on navigation benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing adaptive CBF methods lack formal characterization of how prediction errors from training data propagate through the adaptive pipeline to degrade closed-loop safety guarantees, limiting their reliability in safety-critical applications.
AI.method: Introduces Data-Attributed Adaptive CBF (DA-CBF) framework that integrates TracIn-based data attribution into adaptive CBF learning, with theoretical contributions including corrected safety-loss bounds, safety margin preservation theorem, CBF-QP constraint perturbation bounds, and principled leave-one-out justification for influence-based data curation.
AI.result: On DynamicUnicycle2D benchmark: reduces prediction RMSE by 35.6%, expands certified safe operating set by 39%, and achieves collision-free navigation in 16-obstacle environment where baseline incurs 3 collisions.
AI.conclusion: DA-CBF provides a principled framework for quantifying and mitigating safety degradation from prediction errors in adaptive CBF systems, enabling more reliable safety guarantees through data attribution and theoretical error propagation analysis.

title: Explainable Functional Relation Discovery for Battery State-of-Health Using Kolmogorov-Arnold Network
summary: Battery health management is heavily dependent on reliable State-of-Health (SoH) estimation to ensure battery safety with maximized energy utilization. Although SoH estimation can effectively track battery degradation, it requires continuous battery data acquisition. In addition, model-based SoH estimation methods rely on accurate battery model knowledge, whereas data-driven approaches often suffer from limited interpretability. In contrast, analytical characterization of SoH will offer a direct and tractable handle on battery performance degradation, while also establishing a foundation for further analytical studies toward effective battery health management. Thus, in this work, we propose a Kolmogorov Arnold Network (KAN)-based data-driven pipeline to establish a functional relationship for SoH degradation using battery temperature data. Specifically, we learn long-term battery thermal dynamics and battery heat generation via learnable activation functions of our KAN model. We utilize the learned mapping to obtain an explicit functional relationship between SoH degradation and cycle number. The proposed pipeline was validated using real-world data, yielding a closed-form analytical formula of SoH degradation with high accuracy.

AI.tldr: Proposes a KAN-based data-driven pipeline for analytical SoH degradation modeling using battery temperature data, establishing explicit functional relationships with high accuracy.
AI.motivation: Current SoH estimation methods have limitations: model-based approaches require accurate battery models, data-driven methods lack interpretability, and both need continuous data acquisition. Analytical characterization offers direct, tractable insights into battery degradation for effective health management.
AI.method: Uses Kolmogorov Arnold Network (KAN) with learnable activation functions to model long-term battery thermal dynamics and heat generation from temperature data. Learns mapping to establish explicit functional relationship between SoH degradation and cycle number.
AI.result: Validated with real-world data, yielding a closed-form analytical formula for SoH degradation with high accuracy, providing interpretable degradation modeling.
